modelResponse.episodeSummary: Daniel K. Reeves, Sinus Tachycardia, warning, hemodynamically stable
keyECGEvidence: stDeviation: Diffuse concave (upward-scooping) ST elevation 1-2 mm in leads I, II, aVL, aVF, V3-V6; PR-segment depression in leads II, III, aVF, V4-V6; PR elevation in aVR; ST depression in aVR only; NO reciprocal ST depression in any other lead; ST/T ratio 0.28 in V6
modelResponse.mechanism: Inflammation of the pericardium leading to diffuse ST elevation and PR depression, causing chest pain and sinus tachycardia.
contributingFactors: Recent Upper respiratory infection 1 week ago
Sharp pleuritic chest pain, worse supine, improved leaning forward
Pericardial friction rub heard on auscultation

rejectedAlternatives.why: ST elevation is diffuse and concave (upward-scooping), not localized to a specific coronary territory. No reciprocal ST depression is present, except for ST depression in aVR. Troponin T is only mildly elevated (0.03 ng/mL), not critically high. Pain radiates to trapezius ridge, not typically arm/jaw.
While pleuritic chest pain is present, ECG findings are more typical of pericarditis. No S1Q3T3 pattern or right heart strain signs. BNP is normal (45 pg/mL).

recommendedActions: Administer NSAID (e.g., Ibuprofen 600mg PO Q6H or Indomethacin 25-50mg PO Q8H) for inflammation and pain
Administer Colchicine 0.6mg PO BID for inflammation
Consider high-dose Aspirin (e.g., 650-800mg PO Q6-8H) if NSAIDs contraindicated or ineffective
Monitor ECG for PR normalization and ST/T wave changes
Monitor vital signs and cardiac enzymes
Administer supplemental oxygen if SpO2 drops below 94%
Administer analgesia (e.g., Morphine) for severe pain, cautiously
Rule out underlying causes (e.g., viral, autoimmune)
uncertainty: No prior ECG available for comparison.
Specific viral or autoimmune cause of pericarditis is unknown.
